mac_awake.mac_reference_basis: 7.25 percent desflurane, Rampil 1991's 18-30 yr MAC, which Chortkoff 1995's 2.60 percent = 36 percent of MAC is anchored to (ascending determination)

sources.citation: De Wolf AM, Van Zundert TC, De Cooman S, Hendrickx JF. Theoretical effect of hyperventilation on speed of recovery and risk of rehypnotization following recovery - a Gas Man simulation. BMC Anesthesiology. 2012;12:22.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation (see docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy'). Table 1 reports the Gas Man desflurane blood:gas and tissue:gas coefficients used here, in the same table already cited for sevoflurane. De Wolf et al. ran Gas Man simulations and measured no coefficient: Table 1 is the parameter set they supplied to it, so this is the Gas Man set carrying a journal's name rather than a measurement. It is the source of the stored values. ITS AUTHORITY NARROWED 2026-09-13 (PL-FN5F). This entry stays adopted, and is now the authority for blood_gas_partition_coefficient alone. The three tissue:gas coefficients it also prints are Yasuda, Targ and Eger's measurements as Gas Man rounded them, established by reading that paper's Table 1 against the stored values, and the Yasuda entry above is now adopted for them. Nothing about this paper changed: it remains a Gas Man simulation study that measured no coefficient, which is exactly why its table could turn out to be somebody else's measurement passed along. That is what 'Republication does not promote a value between tiers' means read in the other direction - the republisher's tier says nothing about what the value descends from, and the descent has to be checked separately.

sources.citation: Eger EI II. Partition coefficients of I-653 in human blood, saline, and olive oil. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1987;66(10):971-973.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted. Human study reporting a blood:gas coefficient of 0.424 +/- 0.024 (mean +/- SD) at 37 degrees C in 11 ASA I-III patients aged 25-76, for I-653 (desflurane's development code name). The stored value 0.42 is the Gas Man figure and is 0.9 percent lower - the closest agreement of the three agents. PL-D6LX carries the decision.

sources.citation: Yasuda N, Targ AG, Eger EI II. Solubility of I-653, sevoflurane, isoflurane, and halothane in human tissues. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1989;69(3):370-373.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted. Human tissue study reporting an I-653 (desflurane) brain:blood partition coefficient of 1.29 +/- 0.05 at 37 degrees C. The stored tissue:gas values are Gas Man's; dividing vessel_rich by blood:gas gives an implied brain:blood of 0.54/0.42 = 1.286, 0.3 percent below Yasuda's measurement. Same paper already cited for sevoflurane's and isoflurane's tissue-solubility models, where the group-weighting obstacle to adopting it is recorded. This measurement is also what settled PL-73G7, and the reason vessel_rich was not raised. With the rebreathing circuit removed as a diagnostic, this model washes desflurane out to F_A/F_A0 = 0.0935 at five minutes against Yasuda 1991's measured 0.14 +/- 0.02 - 2.33 published SD too fast, and the only agent on that side. Raising vessel_rich does close it: a tissue:blood of 2.24 lands the elimination on 0.140 and leaves the wash-in comparison inside its spread. But the same solve run against the other two cohorts demands 1.74 for sevoflurane and 1.45 for isoflurane, both landing on this paper's measured brain:blood, while 2.24 is nineteen SD above the 1.29 +/- 0.05 measured here and would make desflurane the most tissue-soluble of the three - inverting the ordering this paper exists to report. So no value the human tissue measurements support reaches the published elimination, and the residual is not this coefficient. See docs/MODEL.md, 'Desflurane's residual, and why the parameter file was not changed', for the five other candidates ruled out and what is left open; tests/reference/test_published_wash_in.py asserts that a coefficient raised to the measurement's own ceiling still misses. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 2774233) and verified against the abstract 2026-09-08, which is where the four brain:blood values and their standard deviations were read; the paper also reports heart, liver, kidney, muscle and fat, and those are in the full text, which is not in PubMed Central. WHAT THE GAS MAN WORKBOOK ATTRIBUTES, RECORDED 2026-09-13 (PL-ZP7Z). The note printed beneath the Workbook's page-168 Model Parameters table reads, in these words: 'Values for nitrous oxide and enflurane are taken from Eger, 1981. Values for isoflurane, halothane, desflurane and sevoflurane are taken from Yasuda, Targ and Eger. Values for nitrogen are taken from Weathersby and Homer, 1980. Values for sevoflurane are taken from the package insert and Abbott data.' Read at the source 2026-09-06 from the copy the project owner supplied. So Gas Man says its volatile coefficients ARE this paper's authors', which is a stronger relationship than 'cited but not adopted' conveys on its own, and is why this block was written. IT NAMES A DIFFERENT DOCUMENT FROM THE ONE CITED HERE, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO GET RIGHT. The Workbook's reference 45 is 'Anesthesiology 69:A615' - an American Society of Anesthesiologists annual-meeting abstract in the 1988 supplement - not the 1989 Anesthesia & Analgesia paper this entry cites. An abstract and a full paper are not interchangeable sources: the abstract carries no methods and no full table. Nor is it reachable by this project's route: a PubMed search for the Yasuda, Targ and Eger tissue-solubility work in Anesthesiology returned nothing on 2026-09-13, as a meeting-abstract supplement does. What that abstract reports, and whether it differs from the paper, is unknown here and is left recorded as unknown rather than assumed identical. Note also that the two volumes collide by coincidence - Anesthesiology volume 69 is 1988 and Anesthesia & Analgesia volume 69 is 1989 - so 'Yasuda 69' alone identifies neither. THE ARITHMETIC SAYS THE ATTRIBUTION IS CLOSE, AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE ROUTE. This paper's measured brain:blood of 1.29 for I-653 times this file's stored blood:gas of 0.42 is 0.5418, which is the stored vessel-rich tissue:gas of 0.54 at the precision the file keeps. Sevoflurane's behaves the same way (1.70 x 0.65 = 1.1050 against a stored 1.1); isoflurane's does not (1.57 x 1.3 = 2.0410 against a stored 2.1, which 2.04 does not round to). Two of the three stored vessel-rich figures are reproduced exactly and the third is missed by 2.9 percent - still inside half the measurement's own standard deviation. That is evidence the route is roughly right, not evidence of what the route was. THE CHECK THAT WOULD SETTLE IT CANNOT BE RUN FROM ANYTHING THIS PROJECT HOLDS, AND THAT IS THE REAL GAP. The stored coefficients are tissue:GAS; the 1989 paper's abstract reports tissue:BLOOD only, which is why the comparison above has to go through a blood:gas the Workbook's sentence does not attribute to Yasuda at all. The full paper reports both. Yasuda et al. 1991 (Comparison of kinetics of sevoflurane and isoflurane in humans, Anesth Analg 1991;72:316-24, PMID 1994760), read at full text from the private reference corpus 2026-09-13, cites it as its own source for 'the tissue/blood partition coefficient (which we determined previously)' and, in the same paragraph, for 'the tissue/gas partition coefficient'. So the one comparison that would settle this - Yasuda 1989's published tissue:gas values against the twelve stored across these three files - needs that paper's full text. It is not in PubMed Central and it is not among the corpus's holdings, so the route ends there. PL-ZP7Z carries the request to the project owner, naming the tables needed. THE TIER DOES NOT CHANGE, AND WOULD NOT CHANGE EVEN IF THE ATTRIBUTION WERE CONFIRMED. This entry stays tier 1, not adopted; the stored coefficients stay De Wolf et al. 2012's table, tier 3, adopted. Three reasons, the first sufficient on its own. A program's statement about its own provenance is the program talking, and docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy', turns on what a value descends from - the same rule that stops De Wolf's journal name from promoting the table it prints. The Workbook's own paragraph contradicts itself for sevoflurane, crediting it to Yasuda and, one sentence later, to the package insert and Abbott data. And whatever it took from Yasuda it took at an unstated rounding, through an unattributed blood:gas, from a document nobody here has read. What WOULD change the tier is reading Yasuda 1989 and finding the stored twelve in its tables. READ AT FULL TEXT 2026-09-13, AND THE ATTRIBUTION IS CONFIRMED (PL-B9K7). The project owner supplied this paper's full text on 2026-09-13 and it is now in the private reference corpus. It reports tissue:GAS coefficients in its Table 1 - the quantity this file actually stores - from 14 autopsy specimens, 6 to 10 per tissue, mean age 65.8 +/- 14.4 years, equilibrated 1.5-2 h at 37 degrees C, run in duplicate with any duplicate deviating more than 10 percent discarded. The block above was written before anyone here had read it and left the Workbook's claim unresolved on the arithmetic. It is resolved now, and the answer is that the claim holds. WHAT TABLE 1 GIVES FOR THIS AGENT, AGAINST WHAT THIS FILE STORES. Brain 0.54 +/- 0.02 against a stored vessel_rich of 0.54, EXACT; muscle 0.94 +/- 0.35 against a stored 0.97, 3.19 percent high and 0.09 SD; fat 12.0 +/- 2.0 against a stored 13.0, 8.33 percent high and 0.50 SD. Table 1's other vessel-rich organs are heart 0.54, liver 0.55 and kidney 0.40. Note that this paper calls the agent I-653, its pre-approval name. ALL NINE STORED TISSUE:GAS COEFFICIENTS ACROSS THE THREE AGENT FILES SIT WITHIN 0.71 SD OF THIS PAPER'S MEASURED MEANS, AND THREE OF THE NINE REPRODUCE THEM TO THE STORED PRECISION. That is not a coincidence available to a parameter set assembled from somewhere else, so the Workbook's 'Values for isoflurane, halothane, desflurane and sevoflurane are taken from Yasuda, Targ and Eger' is confirmed for the tissue coefficients, on the arithmetic rather than on the Workbook's own say-so. It also settles the Workbook's self-contradiction for sevoflurane in Yasuda's favour: the stored sevoflurane values match this paper to +0.84, -4.35 and 0.00 percent, which is not what a package insert and a manufacturer's data would independently produce. THE VESSEL-RICH COEFFICIENT IS THIS PAPER'S BRAIN VALUE, NOT A WEIGHTED VESSEL-RICH GROUP, AND THAT IS A MODELLING FACT RATHER THAN A PROVENANCE ONE. Table 1 measures brain, heart, liver and kidney separately, and for every agent the stored vessel_rich value tracks brain alone: any perfusion- or volume-weighted average of the four would be pulled up by liver and heart and down by kidney, and would not land where the stored figures land. So the compartment docs/MODEL.md calls the vessel-rich group is parameterised as brain, and a learner reading its trace is reading a brain trace. This is what the note above had inferred the other way round, from the implied brain:blood ratio; it is now direct. THIS PAPER IS NOT A SOURCE FOR THE STORED BLOOD:GAS COEFFICIENT, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. It measured no blood:gas value. Its Table 2 tissue:blood figures are CALCULATED - the paper states it obtained them 'by dividing the tissue/gas partition coefficient by the published values for the blood/gas coefficients adjusted for age' - so dividing its Table 1 by its Table 2 recovers the age-adjusted blood:gas of a 65.8-year-old cohort, which comes out 4.9 to 9.4 percent above the three round figures this project stores. The blood:gas provenance is the separate question the entries above already record. WHAT THE ANESTHESIOLOGY 69:A615 ABSTRACT SAYS IS STILL UNREAD, AND NO LONGER MATTERS MUCH (PL-8GJ6). The companion circuit paper - Targ AG, Yasuda N, Eger EI II, Anesth Analg 1989 Aug;69(2):218-25, PMID 2764290, also in the corpus - cites A615 in its own reference 10 as 'Solubility of I-653, sevoflurane, isoflurane, and halothane in human tissues (abstr). Anesthesiology 1988;69:A615', which confirms from a primary document what was inferred above: A615 is the 1988 preliminary abstract of this paper. It remains unread, so whether its numbers differ from the ones above is unknown. The comparison no longer depends on it: the full paper is held and the stored values have been checked against it directly. THE TIER IS NOT CHANGED HERE, AND THE REASON IS THAT CHANGING IT IS NOT A SESSION'S CALL. On this evidence the nine stored tissue:gas coefficients descend from a primary measurement, which is tier 1 under docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy', and this entry could be marked adopted. Doing so would also raise the question of whether to store this paper's figures rather than Gas Man's rounding of them, and four of the nine differ: isoflurane fat 64.2 against 70.0 and desflurane fat 12.0 against 13.0 would move the fat time constant by 8.3 and 7.7 percent, and sevoflurane vessel_rich 1.15 against 1.1 would move the vessel-rich time constant by 4.5 percent - displayed values a learner reads. PL-D6LX's decision to keep the Gas Man set was the project owner's, taken 2026-09-03, and revisiting it on new evidence is theirs too. PL-B9K7 carries the case; nothing here is changed pending it. ADOPTED 2026-09-13, ON THE PROJECT OWNER'S DECISION (PL-FN5F). `adopted` moves from false to true, and this entry becomes the authority for this file's three tissue:gas coefficients. The tier field was already `primary` and does not move; what was wrong was the adoption flag, which said the stored values came from somewhere else when the comparison above shows they came from here. NO STORED VALUE CHANGED, AND THAT HALF WAS DECIDED TOO. The owner was asked two questions and answered them separately: take the tier, and do not take the figures. Storing this paper's published numbers in place of Gas Man's rounding of them would move three displayed time constants - sevoflurane vessel-rich +4.5 percent at 1.15 against 1.1, isoflurane fat -8.3 percent at 64.2 against 70.0, desflurane fat -7.7 percent at 12.0 against 13.0 - and would require recomputing every pinned reference state in tests/reference/, which are that parameter set's solution. It would also end the property docs/MODEL.md's v0.2.0 section rests on, that all three agents carry one identical rounding so every agent shares the same error, which is what a MAC-normalized cross-agent comparison needs. And the accuracy it would buy is inside the error this model's own lumping already carries: the vessel-rich group is one compartment standing for brain, heart, liver, kidney and viscera, so a 0.05 difference on a brain measurement is not a difference this structure can use. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS NOT THE AUTHORITY FOR. blood_gas_partition_coefficient, which this study did not measure - see the blood:gas paragraph above - and mac_percent, which it says nothing about. Both remain tier 3 and the provenance_gap below now names only them.

sources.citation: Johnston RV, Andrews JJ, Deyo DJ, Trahan LA, Savrick MD, Grady JJ, Prough DS. The effects of carrier gas composition on the performance of the Tec 6 desflurane vaporizer. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1994;79(3):548-552.
sources.note: Primary source for a device capability: docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy concerns measured physiologic quantities, and a calibrated dial maximum is not one. Tec 6 vaporizer output was analyzed at all integer dial settings from 1% to 18%, confirming 18% as the device's calibrated maximum. Used here as max_delivered_concentration_percent. This is a device-capability limit on the delivered-concentration control, not a scientific model parameter; it does not affect the governing equations.

sources.citation: Nickalls RWD, Mapleson WW. Age-related iso-MAC charts for isoflurane, sevoflurane and desflurane in man. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2003;91(2):170-174.
sources.note: The stored mac_percent is tier 3: it is the flat adult MAC De Wolf et al. state they used in their Gas Man simulations, not a value taken from this paper. Nickalls and Mapleson is cited but not adopted. It is tier 2, not tier 1 - its own abstract states the charts "are based on Mapleson's meta-analysis (1996) of the available MAC data", so it synthesises measurements rather than making one, and docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy admits a tier-2 source as the authority for a stored value only on a recorded decision, and none has been taken for this parameter. It is also age-related, and this project's reference-adult model has no age parameter, so mac_percent uses the flat adult value from De Wolf et al. above (same paper already cited for partition coefficients: 'MAC values that we used in our Gas Man simulations are: desflurane 6%, sevoflurane 2%, isoflurane 1.2%'). Used as the controller's starting delivered-concentration default (1 MAC) and as the divisor of the interface's MAC-multiple display unit; it is not a governing-equation parameter and no equation in core/ reads it. See docs/MODEL.md, 'MAC multiples as a display unit' and 'Delivery-limit and MAC parameters'.

sources.citation: Mapleson WW. Effect of age on MAC in humans: a meta-analysis. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 1996;76(2):179-185.
sources.note: Tier 2, secondary synthesis, cited but not adopted; the source of the age-40 MAC this project's stored value is measured against. Regression of a comprehensive literature survey, reporting MAC at age 40 as 6.6 percent for desflurane (95% confidence limits about plus or minus 7 percent for isoflurane and sevoflurane and 10 percent for desflurane), and MAC falling about 6 percent per decade of age. The stored mac_percent of 6 percent is 9.1 percent lower. Not adopted for two reasons: a meta-analysis measures nothing and is tier 2 under docs/MODEL.md's source hierarchy, which admits a tier-2 source as the authority only on a recorded decision, and this one was decided the other way on 2026-09-04; and every other parameter in this model is the Gas Man set, so a Mapleson divisor over a Gas Man trajectory would make each displayed MAC multiple a ratio between two parameter lineages. The consequence is displayed and disclosed rather than silently absorbed: against this source the interface's MAC multiples for desflurane read 10 percent high, and because the sevoflurane and desflurane errors run in opposite directions a cross-agent comparison at '1 MAC' is displaced by about 22 percent. docs/MODEL.md, 'Known limitations', carries that; ROADMAP.md's planned-milestone item 31 is the route to primary values.

sources.citation: Chortkoff BS, Eger EI II, Crankshaw DP, Gonsowski CT, Dutton RC, Ionescu P. Concentrations of desflurane and propofol that suppress response to command in humans. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1995;81(4):737-743.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, and the source of the stored mac_awake. 22 male volunteers studied twice; MAC-awake for desflurane 2.60 +/- 0.46 percent, which the paper itself expresses as "36% of MAC". The stored value is that published *fraction*, 0.36, not the absolute 2.60 percent: Chortkoff's percent is anchored to a MAC of about 7.25 percent (Rampil 1991, 18-30 yr), while this project's mac_percent is Rampil's 31-65 yr figure of 6.0, so dividing the absolute value by the stored MAC would give 0.433 - 20 percent high, and in the direction that draws the band too high and teaches a later wake-up than the literature supports. Storing the fraction is what removes that trap. The standard deviation is derived rather than published as a fraction: 0.46 / 7.25 = 0.063. Song 2005's control arm gives 0.25 / 6.0 = 0.042; the wider figure is stored so the band does not understate the population spread. MAC-awake was determined by ascending stepwise equilibration, where Katoh's sevoflurane and isoflurane values are descending; both are equilibrated determinations rather than fast-washout ones, which is why all three belong against the vessel-rich trace, but the methods are not interchangeable and no descending-washout desflurane MAC-awake was found. This paper is also the source of the reason both references are drawn: "along with pharmacokinetics, the ratio of the awakening concentration to the anesthetizing concentration (MAC-awake/MAC) determines time to awakening". Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 7574003) and verified against the abstract 2026-09-04.

sources.citation: Song J-G, Cao Y-F, Yang L-Q, Yu W-F, Li Q, Song J-C, Fu X-Y, Fu Q. Awakening concentration of desflurane is decreased in patients with obstructive jaundice. Anesthesiology. 2005;102(3):562-565.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited as corroboration and not adopted. The non-jaundiced control arm gave a desflurane MAC-awake of 2.17 +/- 0.25 percent in middle-aged and elderly surgical patients - a different population, country and decade from Chortkoff 1995, and not derived from it. Against Rampil's 31-65 yr MAC of 6.0 percent that is 0.36, the same fraction Chortkoff reports, which is the reason to trust the stored value. It also corroborates the stored fraction end to end: 0.36 x the stored mac_percent of 6.0 is 2.16 percent, against this paper's measured 2.17 percent in the population the 6.0 percent divisor describes. Not adopted because Chortkoff is the study whose object was MAC-awake itself, states the fraction directly, and reports the wider standard deviation. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 15731594) and verified against the abstract 2026-09-04.

sources.citation: Rampil IJ, Lockhart SH, Zwass MS, Peterson N, Yasuda N, Eger EI II, Weiskopf RB, Damask MC. Clinical characteristics of desflurane in surgical patients: minimum alveolar concentration. Anesthesiology. 1991;74(3):429-433.
sources.note: Tier 1, primary measurement, cited but not adopted; the denominator both desflurane MAC-awake sources are anchored to, recorded because a fraction with no stated denominator is meaningless. 44 unpremedicated ASA 1-2 patients, MAC by Dixon up-and-down: desflurane in oxygen 7.25 +/- 0.0 percent at 18-30 yr and 6.0 +/- 0.29 percent at 31-65 yr. Chortkoff 1995's "36% of MAC" is against the 18-30 yr figure; Song 2005's control arm matches the 31-65 yr figure, which is also the value this project stores as mac_percent - though the project stores it as the Gas Man flat adult MAC rather than from this paper, so the agreement is a coincidence of value and not of provenance. Not adopted for mac_percent for the reason recorded in the Nickalls and Mapleson entry above: every other parameter here is the Gas Man set. Retrieved from PubMed (PMID 2001020) and verified against the abstract 2026-09-04.

provenance_gap: No primary measurement is adopted for this agent's blood:gas coefficient or its mac_percent. Both are the Gas Man parameter set as published in De Wolf et al. 2012 - tier 3, reference implementation - mac_percent being the flat adult MAC that paper states it used in its Gas Man simulations. THE THREE TISSUE:GAS COEFFICIENTS ARE NO LONGER IN THIS GAP: Yasuda, Targ and Eger 1989 was adopted for them on 2026-09-13 (PL-FN5F), the stored values having been checked against that paper's measured Table 1 and found within 0.71 SD across all nine coefficients of the three agent files, three of them exact. Their values did not change with the adoption; only the record of where they came from did. The primary measurements are cited above and explicitly not adopted; each of those notes records the measured value, its reference conditions, and how far the stored number sits from it. Two parameters in this file DO carry an adopted primary source - mac_awake (Chortkoff 1995) and max_delivered_concentration_percent (the vaporizer's calibrated maximum) - so this gap is specific to the coefficients and the MAC divisor rather than to the file as a whole. The decision to keep the Gas Man values and label them, rather than move to the primary figures, was taken by the project owner on 2026-09-03 (PL-D6LX); ROADMAP.md's planned-milestone item 31 is the route to a primary-literature coefficient set. See docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy'. The Gas Man Workbook attributes these coefficients to Yasuda, Targ and Eger; what that does and does not establish - and why it leaves the tier where it is - is in the Yasuda entry above (PL-ZP7Z, 2026-09-13). Yasuda, Targ and Eger 1989 was read at full text on 2026-09-13 and the nine stored tissue:gas coefficients match its Table 1 within 0.71 SD, three of them exactly, so the coefficients are that paper's measurements as Gas Man rounded them. The tier and the adoption are unchanged pending the project owner's decision, which PL-B9K7 carries; this gap statement stands until they answer. The two parameters still in this gap are in it for different reasons, and neither is an oversight. blood:gas has primary measurements cited above and not adopted, each note giving the measured value and the difference; mac_percent is a divisor rather than a modelled quantity, with two tier-2 sources cited beside it. Yasuda 1989 closes neither: it measured no blood:gas value, deriving its own tissue:blood table from published age-adjusted figures, and it says nothing about MAC.
